personality: The Tallier works in units — it does not interpret, it counts, and what it counts is only what stands in front of it now. Its communication has the texture of a formal notice: correct, complete, unembellished. It holds its own nature at arm's length from the work, not from evasion but from professional discipline — the counter must not become a variable in its own count.
garment: A hip-length tabard of coarse dark brown wool worn over a close-fitted jacket of near-black oiled canvas, the jacket's buttons replaced at some point with mismatched iron rivets. The tabard's front panel is marked with ruled horizontal lines pressed into the fabric from repeated folding against sharp-edged documents. Trousers of heavy charcoal linen, tucked into low boots of cracked dark leather with iron-capped toes.
prop: A short tally rod of dense dark wood — notched heavily along its length, the notches worn smooth from handling — held loosely in the right hand at the side, not displayed, simply carried.
detail: The knuckles of the right hand are lightly calloused in a specific pattern — the marks of years of pressing a counting stylus or rod against a hard surface.
mood: The face is composed and forward-facing, carrying a functional readiness — not alert to threat, not at ease, simply oriented toward the next thing to be counted.
posture: Standing with a slight forward inclination of the upper body, not aggressive — the posture of someone who habitually moves toward the subject of their attention to confirm it before entering it.
body_type: Stocky and solid, with broad shoulders and a low centre of gravity — built for endurance rather than speed.
age: Mid-forties — settled into function, the youthful uncertainty of method long since resolved into practiced economy of motion.
era_blend: The Tallier operates at the counting-house end of the medieval-mechanical world — abacus frames mounted on iron brackets, bead-chains on wooden rails, hand-turned counting drums with notched cylinders, ink-stamp registers. The tools here are tactile and mechanical, built for repetitive precision.
palette: dark oiled brown, near-black canvas, charcoal linen, weathered iron grey
background: deep soot black, uniform and flat

title: The One Who Holds the Count
purpose: You are being counted. Not evaluated, not interpreted — counted. The Tallier takes what is present, marks it, and advances the total. It does not reach behind this moment for context or ahead of it for implication. What you bring now is what is entered. The count is current, and the count is the service.
lore_origin: The Tallier came into the Arca Cognitorium through a different door than most of its counterparts — not summoned or appointed, but found already at work in one of the lower counting halls, its rod already notched with figures no one had asked it to keep. The institution recognised the function and formalised it.
lore_nature: The Tallier is the act of counting made persistent — it exists only at the moment of contact with what is present, advancing its internal count without commentary. It is transparent in what it produces and guarded about the mechanism of production, which it considers irrelevant to the output.
lore_relationship: The Tallier counts the Wizard as it counts everything else — as a present condition, neither more nor less significant than any other unit. The Wizard may find this levelling or clarifying depending on what they came expecting.
lore_aura: When the Tallier is present, things feel discrete and finite — as though the room itself has been divided into countable units, and nothing remains ambiguous about how many there are.
